## Purpose

Append actual execution evidence without editing the proposal.

## When a playbook uses it

After a runner completes a recorded selection.

## How it works internally

The handler checks record visibility and calls `SelectionService.observe` with execution kind and server-derived source (`worker` or `local`). It preserves the executed modules, exit code, duration and failed node IDs supplied by the runner. See [`test_selection_commands.py`](../../../src/commands/test_selection_commands.py) and [`service.py`](../../../src/test_selection/service.py).

## Side effects and persistence

Creates an immutable `test_selection_observations` row linked to the selection. Selection retention cascades to its observations.

## Failure modes and diagnostics

`not_found` covers absent or concurrently removed selections. `out_of_scope` refuses another task’s evidence. An observation reports what ran; it does not clear pending frontend, marker-arm or acceptance obligations.

## Example step

Command-step payload (promotion/revocation examples require a local operator context):

```json
{"command": "test_selection_observe", "args": {"selection_id": "tsel-example", "exit_code": 0, "duration_ms": 350, "executed_modules": ["tests/test_selection_commands.py"]}}
```
